asks: Asks the commission to keep electoral boundaries that firmly separate rural and urban areas, keep Livingstone-Macleod as it is, and not mix part of Lethbridge with rural areas.

quote: Well, I don’t think it would land very well. I think that it would confuse the voters. I think it would water down the effectiveness of the MLA that had to deal with that issue.
note: Answer to Mr. Clark's question: 'if we were to, say, create constituencies that would bite off a piece of Lethbridge and make it mixed with rural, how would that land'. Presenter is a Lethbridge resident and also asks for 'a marked delineation between rural and urban ridings'. Rejection is of a generic Lethbridge hybrid (L3, and L2 by direction). Text-layer order jumbled; quote falls between EB-4 and EB-7 labels.
Airdrie named only as an example of a fast-growing new city.
'northern Alberta, like Slave Lake and those areas' named only as an example of vast rural districts.

asks: Asks the commission to respect municipal boundaries and like communities and keep Livingstone-Macleod and its name as they are, not subsumed by Lethbridge.

quote: The softening of that language makes me concerned as a rural person because the idea of being subsumed by Lethbridge is horrifying.
note: Livingstone-Macleod (Bellevue) resident rejecting her rural area being joined with Lethbridge; L2 would put Crowsnest Pass and Fort Macleod with a quarter of the city. The Chair's summary 'you do not want to be lumped in with Lethbridge' is not answered with a direct yes. No want stated for the city itself.

asks: Asks, for the MD of Taber council, that boundaries reflect the rural lifestyle and keep two MLAs across the Oldman River without reaching to Strathmore for numbers; personally prefers an east-west alignment and worries about four Lethbridge-anchored ridings.

quote: I do worry that you could have four representatives from the city of Lethbridge.
note: Reacting to an earlier presenter's diagram of four Lethbridge spoke ridings; Mr. Clark asks 'You don't like the four sort of . . .' and she answers. Just before, she says 'I do catch my breath when I see that diagram.' No EB label precedes the passage in this record.
Chestermere named only as part of the federal Bow River riding, as an example of an immense riding.

asks: Asks that urban municipal boundaries such as Lethbridge's be respected as far as reasonable, that rural communities not be stretched too far, and that Indigenous communities not be divided.

quote: I do believe that when we look, especially with urban boundaries within Alberta here and especially here in Lethbridge, we are a growing community.
note: The request follows: urban issues 'be respected and that the boundaries be respected as much as reasonably possible'. Read as keeping Lethbridge's ridings within the city boundary (L1 direction). He also muses the city might get one of the new seats, which would be more city seats rather than L1 exactly. No EB label in record.

asks: Asks that Lethbridge have two representatives within the city's boundaries, with any rural territory in Lethbridge-West returned to the Macleod area and no rural areas added to the city.

quote: redistribution by restricting Lethbridge to having two representatives within the urban geographic boundaries and without outlying rural territories would accommodate for the population growth that Lethbridge has experienced
note: Rejection quote (EB-11): 'what I would not understand is changing the electoral boundaries to add rural areas to the city of Lethbridge' and 'carving out Lethbridge-West and adding in other rural territories, dilutes the democratic legitimacy of Lethbridge voters'. She believed Coalhurst was in Lethbridge-West; Mr. Evans corrects her that it is not.
'Slave Lake' named only as an example of a district with under half the average population.

asks: Asks the commission to honour the urban-rural divide, draw rural ridings that make geographic and cultural sense (citing Crowsnest Pass/Ranchland and Cardston-Siksika as problems), and resist mixing wedges of Lethbridge with rural southern Alberta.

quote: let’s take a portion of Lethbridge and put a big wedge of the rest of southern Alberta, and it will all come down to Lethbridge, and it’ll make the numbers, and it’ll look really good. Well, that’s what I call the Costco version of redistricting.
note: Also: 'you have to resist the temptation to turn those ridings into a mixed riding. They will be buried, and they will be lost.' Asked by the Chair 'are you for or against blended ridings?' he answers 'I'm against them. They don't work.' Wedges into Lethbridge resemble the four-way plan (L2) and any hybrid (L3). No want stated for the city.

asks: Asks the commission to stress population, clear boundaries and municipal communities of interest, follow the data toward Calgary and Edmonton, avoid rurban districts, and not create a third Lethbridge constituency or fold Coalhurst or Coaldale into the city.

quote: given the previous statements and understanding of Calgary and Edmonton combined with the data of Lethbridge-West and Lethbridge-East, Lethbridge neither needs nor deserves another constituency.
note: Rejection quote, same pages: 'When you take part of a large urban centre to create a rurban, rural-urban, district, you fail to understand or respect the fact that the residents in both the urban and rural communities have different cultures', illustrated with Coalhurst, Picture Butte, Lethbridge County versus Lethbridge. Also says adding Coalhurst or Coaldale to the city 'would rub them wrong'. Want read as keeping Lethbridge's two city ridings.
'Sylvan Lake is not Red Deer' named only as an example of distinct municipalities.
Rocky Mountain House named only as an example ('nor is it Rocky Mountain House'); no stance on the riding.

asks: Asks the commission not to change the boundaries of Lethbridge-East and Lethbridge-West.

quote: I guess that my last comment to you is: please don’t change the boundaries in Lethbridge.
note: Chair asks 'Both west and east: is that what you're saying?' and she answers 'West and east.' Former MLA for Lethbridge-East. The later passage labelled 'Ms Fitzpatrick' about 13th Street and keeping the ridings within Lethbridge is Belinda Crowson's testimony (the Chair thanks 'Ms Crowson'), so not coded here.

asks: Gives the history of Lethbridge's urban-only ridings and the 13th Street divide, implicitly asking that the city's ridings stay within the city and keep 13th Street for now.

quote: so we have had a riding that has only been urban since 1909. We have never included rural areas since 1909, a long precedence for our community.
note: Her explicit request ('to me that boundary of keeping it only within Lethbridge makes not only sense today, but it makes historic sense') is printed inside HANSARD-R1-T02-006 under a 'Ms Fitzpatrick' label; the Chair then thanks 'Ms Crowson'. Within this record the want is carried by the historical argument; she also says 13th Street is a natural divide for now.

asks: Asks that city boundaries be respected, with two constituencies wholly inside Lethbridge (shifting the internal line to the highway), one urban plus one blended seat for smaller cities like Airdrie on the St. Albert model, Calgary and Edmonton seats inside their limits, and a Cardston-Taber-Warner / Little Bow pair around Lethbridge.

quote: For Lethbridge, specifically, I want two constituencies completely contained within the city. No sharing with bedroom communities.
note: Also proposes moving the internal East/West line north of St. Basil's from 13th Street to Stafford Drive and the highway, roughly 3,000 people.

quote: I think St. Albert and Grande Prairie, the constituencies they have right now, are the template that probably should be followed for communities like Airdrie and Medicine Hat.
note: Preceded by: 'for the smaller cities, in my opinion, I would like one urban and then one blended constituency'. For Airdrie this is one Airdrie-only seat plus one Airdrie-and-rural seat, which matches none of A1-A4 exactly.

quote: I think St. Albert and Grande Prairie, the constituencies they have right now, are the template that probably should be followed
note: Endorses the current St. Albert pattern (one urban, one blended) as a model for other cities; offered as a template rather than a request about St. Albert itself.
'Red Deer currently is also roughly 2' stated in his population tally next to Lethbridge; he implies two city seats but makes no request about Red Deer. Coded as mention under rule 17.

asks: Asks the commission to maintain the boundaries of Lethbridge-West and Lethbridge-East within the city, not combine any part of Lethbridge with rural areas, and focus instead on over-populated Calgary and Edmonton ridings.

quote: There are four important reasons I’d like to highlight to maintain the boundaries for Lethbridge-West and Lethbridge-East.
note: Rejection quote (EB-20): 'Combining any part of the city of Lethbridge with the rural areas or smaller municipalities would really do nothing to ensure appropriate representation for residents of Lethbridge.' Also: focus on large urban ridings 'rather than creating rural-urban, or rurban, constituencies'. MLA for Lethbridge-West.
'Lesser Slave Lake is, like, 16,000, 17,000 people' named only as an example of a small rural riding.

asks: Asks the commission to leave Lethbridge's two ridings and lines as they are, not pull in neighbouring bedroom communities or rural areas, and focus on Calgary and Edmonton growth.

quote: So I would urge the commission to leave Lethbridge ultimately alone, leave these lines alone, and move to the bigger issues
note: Rejection quote (before EB-23): 'For Lethbridge, if you chose to tinker, I would hope that that would not include a tinkering including outside neighbouring bedroom communities.' Also opposes pulling outlying rural areas into urban ridings.

asks: Asks that Lethbridge keep at least two constituencies entirely within the city, as on the current map, and not be joined with Coaldale, Coalhurst, Stirling, Raymond or other rural areas.

quote: I think that Lethbridge should maintain at least two constituencies which are entirely contained within the boundaries of the city of Lethbridge, so that map that’s displayed right there, that’s just fine with me
note: Rejection: 'having a boundary that involves Coaldale, Coalhurst, Sterling, Raymond, whatever it is in a riding that also includes big chunks of Lethbridge, that really, I think, takes away from the representational capacity'. 'At least two' leaves room for more city seats, but he endorses the current map.

Says city-only seats for a mid-sized city like Lethbridge matter, 'even extrapolating to places like Red Deer, Medicine Hat'. An extension by example, not a request about Red Deer; coded as mention (rule 17).

asks: Asks the commission to merge Lethbridge-East and Lethbridge-West with surrounding rural areas into four blended ridings (Lethbridge-Livingstone, -Little Bow, -Taber, -Cardston), eliminating Cardston-Siksika, on the Medicine Hat hybrid model.

quote: My proposal is to merge the existing Lethbridge-East and Lethbridge-West with surrounding rural areas to create four blended ridings, shown here as Lethbridge-Livingstone, Lethbridge-Little Bow, Lethbridge-Taber and Lethbridge-Cardston.
note: Rejection of the current city-only pair (EB-25): 'Lethbridge's current electoral division risks entrenching urban-rural divides by carving out the city into isolated segments'. Asked by Mrs. Samson (EB-31) about leaving Lethbridge stand-alone, he answers 'I don't think that would be as effective.' Gives city cut lines (6th Ave/Whoop-Up Drive, Mayor Magrath Drive) and populations 52,000-64,000. A passage of Mrs. Miyanaga's testimony is interleaved in this record and not coded here.

asks: Asks, for Cardston County council, that the north-south 'figure eight' Cardston-Siksika riding be replaced with an east-west southern riding like the old Cardston-Taber-Warner.

note: On the evening's talk of Lethbridge rural-urban mixing he says 'I don't know how I feel about that. I know that could work'. No stance. The record's tail (Chair questioning Mr. Mills) is not his testimony.

asks: Asks for minimal change, populations close to the median, geographic district names, Edmonton-Mill Woods kept whole by community league (adding all of Ridgewood), Edmonton-Ellerslie wholly south of the Henday, more seats for Edmonton and Calgary, and no urban-rural hybrid ridings.

note: 'Rimbey-Rocky Mountain House-Sundre' named only as an example of a descriptive district name.

'Olds-Didsbury-Three Hills' named only as an example of a descriptive district name. His opposition to hybrids for 'some of the cities in southern Alberta' names no city, so LETHBRIDGE is not coded (rule 1).

asks: For the Alberta Federation of Labour, asks the commission to use the most current provincial population estimates (ideally 2026 census data) so that voter parity holds, especially in fast-growing Calgary, Edmonton and Airdrie-Cochrane ridings.

note: Airdrie-Cochrane named only as one of nine ridings with 20-52% growth since 2017.
Airdrie-Cochrane named only as one of nine ridings with 20-52% growth since 2017.

asks: Asks that Spruce Grove-Stony Plain be split, with Stony Plain joined to Drayton Valley and a Spruce Grove-Edmonton hybrid riding taking in west Edmonton subdivisions, and supports blended ridings generally.

note: Cochrane named only in a list of fast-growing suburban communities.
Chestermere named only in a list of fast-growing suburban communities.
Says there is little demographic difference between St. Albert and northwest Edmonton, as an argument for blended ridings in general; no request about St. Albert's districts.

asks: Asks the commission to keep urban ridings from growing too large (perhaps more city seats), avoid hybrid ridings that dilute rural voices, and never gerrymander.
